Almost all of us will experience reproductive health issues at some point in our working lives.

It can impact us, our friends and our family in big ways, and it's costing our economy billions in lost productivity as well.

Here's how reproductive health leave can make a big difference for working Australians.

Lets get it into the National Employment Standard for every worker. #itsforeverybody

A year ago Jarrod Bleijie promised to protect retail workers from violence at work. A year on, and he's delivered nothing.

Queensland is now the last state in the country to move on workplace protection orders. Every other state has either legislated, drafted or consulted. We've gone from the front of the pack on workplace safety to lagging behind.

This is happening while workers are being threatened with death over 20 grams of ham, and spat on for refusing to serve a drunk customer. 

One in four retail workers are assaulted at work.

Why does this Crisafulli LNP Government fail Queenslanders on workplace safety every single time?

Two years ago, Queensland led the way by introducing paid Reproductive Health Leave for many public sector workers. Now, we want to know how it's working in practice. 

If you currently have access to Reproductive Health Leave, we want to hear from you. Whether you've used the entitlement or not, your experience will help build the evidence we need to campaign for something we believe should be available to every worker in Australia. 

Our anonymous survey only takes a few minutes to complete, but your voice will help shape the future of workplace rights, improve support for workers, and strengthen the case for expanding this important entitlement nationwide. 

Because reproductive health affects all of us, in different ways, at different times. 

It should be for Everybody. Complete our survey: https://qcu.link/ifebsurvey

The Crisafulli-Bleijie Government is trying to weaken workplace health and safety laws.

Safety should never be sacrificed in the name of productivity or cutting red tape.

It was great to meet with Tamika and Dinisha from the @unitedworkersoz in support of the @queenslandunions ‘Hands Off our Safety’ campaign.
